prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were hurt — that’s stressful. I can help you pick the right lawyer, but first a few quick questions so my advice is tailored:

- How serious are your injuries (minor, require surgery, long-term disability)?
- Was the other driver clearly at fault? Were police/insurance involved?
- Do you already have an insurer/adjuster talking to you?
- Do you prefer a big firm, a smaller boutique firm, or an attorney who will go to trial if needed?
- Any language preference or budget concerns?

If you just want immediate general guidance, here’s what to look for and do right away.

What type of lawyer you should hire
- A California personal injury attorney who handles auto collisions and has trial experience. If you have catastrophic injuries, look for a lawyer experienced with catastrophic or brain/spine injury cases.

Key qualifications and experience
- Licensed in California and in good standing with the State Bar (you can verify at https://www.calbar.ca.gov).
- Regularly handles car-accident cases and knows Alameda County courts and local medical providers.
- Has a track record of settlements and trial verdicts (ask for examples in consultation).
- Experience with your injury type (e.g., orthopedic surgeon referrals, wrongful death, soft-tissue vs catastrophic).

Practical factors to compare
- Contingency fee (common range 33%–40% plus costs; get fees in writing).
- How they communicate (who you’ll talk to, expected response times).
- Whether they advance medical/ litigation costs and handle medical liens.
- Trial willingness — many cases settle, but some require trial; ask their trial rate.
- Local presence — Pleasanton/Alameda County experience helps with local courts, doctors, and investigators.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- Do you handle mainly car-accident cases or other practice areas?
- What percentage of your cases settle vs go to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (similar injuries/fault scenario)?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What are your fees and what costs will I be responsible for?
- What results have you achieved recently for similar cases?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or “easy huge settlement.”
- Pressure to sign immediately without time to review the retainer.
- Poor communication in the consult or evasive answers about experience.
- Unlicensed attorney or disciplinary history.

Immediate steps to protect your claim
- Seek and follow medical care — medical records are key evidence.
- Preserve evidence (photos, vehicle damage, contact info of witnesses).
- Do not give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without your lawyer.
- Be aware of the statute of limitations: generally 2 years in California for personal injury lawsuits (file sooner rather than later). Claims against a public entity have much shorter notice requirements.

How I can help right now
- I can search for and provide a short list (3–5) of personal injury lawyers or firms near Pleasanton with good reputations and relevant experience.
- I can draft an email or script you can use in initial calls.
- I can create a checklist to compare lawyers after consultations.

Tell me whether you want me to find local lawyers (and whether you have any preferences), or answer any of the questions above so I can give more specific recommendations.
